!*> Setup
!include .EDS.Setup
!define REST_ROOT {[ http(s)://HOST:PORT/ROOT ]}

*!

!anchor content
!1 !-<img src="files/javadog.png"> API - Application Programming Interface -!
The EDS API consists of 2 main parts, the first is the management part, which
is used to control a EDS instance, and the second is the sharing part. The full
documentation of the API is its contract, ''openapi.json'' (in the module eds-api), which a
running EDS also serves as ${REST_ROOT}/openapi.json.

There was both a SOAP & REST based !-WebService-! available, the default for
the !-FitNesse-! tests is the REST, if the SOAP based !-WebServices-! are still
required, please use version 1.2, as that is the final version with SOAP
support, as of 2.0 SOAP support has been discontinued.

Note; EDS is not a HTTP(S) Server, it is an Application, the JSON requests will
therefore always return the standard HTTP code 200, whenever an incoming request
has been answered by the EDS. A different !-ReturnCode-! & !-ReturnMessage-! is
set in the response, which will provide more details if the request could not
be processed correctly. The EDS !-ReturnCodes-! are similar to the HTTP codes,
so understanding them should be easier, but the !-ReturnMessage-! is containing
significantly more details regarding the problem. This was decided to ensure
that a System using EDS can better deal with the problems without having to
resort to EDS logs. The streaming of content, the Resource API, the Features and the
Status are the exception: they answer with the return code as HTTP status.

[[Management has the following elements: ][#management]]

 * '''[[ Version ][#version]] '''
 * '''[[ !-MasterKey-! ][#masterkey]] '''
 * '''[[ Settings ][#settings]] '''
 * '''[[ Sanitized ][#sanitized]] '''
 * '''[[ Authenticated ][#authenticated]] '''
 * '''[[ Members ][#members]] '''
 * '''[[ Circles of Trust ][#circles]] '''
 * '''[[ Trustees ][#trustees]] '''
 * '''[[ Status ][#status]] '''

[[ Sharing has the following elements: ][#sharing]]

 * '''[[ Data Type ][#datatype]] '''
 * '''[[ Data ][#data]] '''
 * '''[[ Content Streaming ][#streaming]] '''
 * '''[[ Resource API ][#resources]] '''
 * '''[[ Features ][#features]] '''

----
[[ Top ][#content]]
!anchor management
!2 Management
Management primarily contain the functionality which is used to control
the system, including altering settings. Adding a system specific !-MasterKey-!
as well as creating Members, Circles of Trust and assign Members as Trustees to
the Circles.

'''Important'''; ''A new EDS has no account at all, and so no default name or
passphrase which someone could forget to change. The very first request claims it:
its account name and passphrase become the System Administrator. The passphrase
must be strong enough, like every passphrase in EDS. For this test, the setup claims
the instance as '''admin''', with the passphrase ${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}.''

!* Version
[[ Top ][#content]]
!anchor version
!4 '''Version'''
Returns the current Version of the running EDS instance. This method serves
mainly as a simply way to check if the system is operational. This request is
the only EDS request not requiring any credentials to invoke.

 * Version - Read version of running instance, act as ping
   * REST (POST) request is: ${REST_ROOT}/version

|version                                  |
|return code?|return message?|eds version?|
|${SUCCESS}  |Ok             |2.0-SNAPSHOT|
*!

!* !-MasterKey-!
[[ Top ][#content]]
!anchor masterkey
!4 '''!-MasterKey-!'''
The !-MasterKey-! is the kill-switch of !-EDS-!. It is not stored anywhere: it is
derived (HKDF-SHA512) from an external high-entropy source when !-EDS-! starts,
and lives only in memory. The database only holds its version and a key check
value, so a wrong !-MasterKey-! is rejected without decrypting anything. There is
no default !-MasterKey-!: without a source (the environment variable
'''EDS_MASTERKEY_URL''' or the setting '''eds.masterkey.url'''), !-EDS-! stays
locked, until it is unlocked with the !-MasterKey-! request. On a fresh instance,
the first request sets the !-MasterKey-! up. The Setup page does this.

To make sure the next test run also works, the !-MasterKey-! is reverted to the
original at the end of the following table.

 * !-MasterKey-! - Unlock & Set !-MasterKey-!
   * Only '''System Administrators''' may perform this
   * REST (POST) request is: ${REST_ROOT}/masterKey

|master key                                                                                              |
|account name|credential|url                                 |secret|return code?|return message?        |
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|null                                |${MASTERKEY_DEFAULT}|${SUCCESS}  |!-MasterKey-! unlocked.|
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|null                                |${MASTERKEY_SECRET}|${SUCCESS}  |!-MasterKey-! updated. |
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|null                                |admin |${VERIFICATION_WARNING}|The !-MasterKey-! secret is too weak. Use at least 20 random characters (letters, digits and symbols), or a passphrase of several random words.|
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|null                                |${MASTERKEY_DEFAULT}|${SUCCESS}  |!-MasterKey-! updated. |

The secret may instead be read from a URL (the column url), a file or a web address; this isn't tested here, as the test
must not depend on a source outside it.

Changing the !-MasterKey-! rotates it: everything it protects (the Members' keys and the Trustees' Circle Secrets) is re-wrapped
with the new !-MasterKey-! in one transaction, sessions end and pending invitations are deleted. Data Objects aren't touched. A new
!-MasterKey-! secret must be strong enough.

!* Settings
[[ Top ][#content]]
!anchor settings
!4 '''Settings'''
The !-EDS-! Settings request can only be performed by the System
Administrator, i.e. the system super user. It is a way to both extract the
current settings, and update existing values.

 * Settings - Read & Update Settings
   * Only '''System Administrators''' may perform this
   * REST (POST) request is: ${REST_ROOT}/settings

|script|Settings     |admin                          |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|
|show  |value for key|eds.crypto.symmetric.algorithm |
|show  |value for key|eds.crypto.asymmetric.algorithm|
|show  |value for key|eds.crypto.pbe.algorithm       |
|show  |value for key|eds.crypto.hash.algorithm      |
|show  |value for key|eds.system.locale              |
|show  |value for key|eds.system.charset             |
|show  |value for key|eds.show.all.circles           |
|show  |value for key|eds.show.trustees              |
|show  |value for key|eds.sanity.check.startup       |
|show  |value for key|eds.sanity.check.interval.days |
|show  |value for key|eds.cors.value                 |
|show  |value for key|eds.circle.secret.rotation.days|
|show  |value for key|eds.circle.secret.rotation.threads|

The values above are only shown, not checked: they depend on the defaults and on
what is stored in the database, and are there for information.

Note, that if a different user attempts to invoke this request, it is refused, and
the list has only undefined values.

|script|Settings     |user1                          |${PASSPHRASE_1}|
|check |return code  |${AUTHORIZATION_WARNING}       |
|check |value for key|eds.crypto.symmetric.algorithm |undefined|
|check |value for key|eds.crypto.asymmetric.algorithm|undefined|
|check |value for key|eds.crypto.pbe.algorithm       |undefined|
|check |value for key|eds.crypto.hash.algorithm      |undefined|
|check |value for key|eds.system.locale              |undefined|
|check |value for key|eds.system.charset             |undefined|
|check |value for key|eds.show.all.circles           |undefined|
|check |value for key|eds.show.trustees              |undefined|
|check |value for key|eds.sanity.check.startup       |undefined|
|check |value for key|eds.sanity.check.interval.days |undefined|
|check |value for key|eds.cors.value                 |undefined|
|check |value for key|eds.circle.secret.rotation.days|undefined|

!5 Symmetric Algorithm
The primary part of all internal encryption is performed using Symmetric Keys. These are all based on the AES algorithms
and only AES-256-GCM is supported (CNSA 2.0 / BSI TR-02102). The CBC variants and the 128 and 192 bit key sizes
were removed in EDS 2.0.
The allowed values are:
 * '''AES_GCM_256'''

|Settings                                                                                                                                                            |
|account name|credential|key                           |value      |return code?      |return message?                                                   |defined?   |
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|eds.crypto.symmetric.algorithm|AES_CBC_128|${SETTING_WARNING}|Unsupported Crypto Algorithm for 'eds.crypto.symmetric.algorithm'.|AES_GCM_256|
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|eds.crypto.symmetric.algorithm|AES_CBC_192|${SETTING_WARNING}|Unsupported Crypto Algorithm for 'eds.crypto.symmetric.algorithm'.|AES_GCM_256|
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|eds.crypto.symmetric.algorithm|AES_CBC_256|${SETTING_WARNING}|Unsupported Crypto Algorithm for 'eds.crypto.symmetric.algorithm'.|AES_GCM_256|
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|eds.crypto.symmetric.algorithm|AES_GCM_128|${SETTING_WARNING}|Unsupported Crypto Algorithm for 'eds.crypto.symmetric.algorithm'.|AES_GCM_256|
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|eds.crypto.symmetric.algorithm|AES_GCM_192|${SETTING_WARNING}|Unsupported Crypto Algorithm for 'eds.crypto.symmetric.algorithm'.|AES_GCM_256|
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|eds.crypto.symmetric.algorithm|AES_GCM_256|${SUCCESS}        |Ok                                                                |AES_GCM_256|
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|eds.crypto.symmetric.algorithm|AES_CBC_512|${SETTING_WARNING}|Unsupported Crypto Algorithm for 'eds.crypto.symmetric.algorithm'.|AES_GCM_256|

!5 Asymmetric Algorithm
Each Member Account has its own key pairs, which are used to wrap the Circle keys. Since !-EDS-! 2.0, these are a hybrid of
ML-KEM-1024 (post-quantum) and ECDH P-384: both must be broken to recover a Circle key. RSA was removed.
The allowed values are:
 * '''MLKEM1024_P384'''

|Settings                                                                                                                                                        |
|account name|credential|key                            |value   |return code?      |return message?                                                    |defined?|
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|eds.crypto.asymmetric.algorithm|MLKEM1024_P384|${SUCCESS}        |Ok                                                                 |MLKEM1024_P384|
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|eds.crypto.asymmetric.algorithm|RSA_2048|${SETTING_WARNING}|Unsupported Crypto Algorithm for 'eds.crypto.asymmetric.algorithm'.|MLKEM1024_P384|

!5 PBE Algorithm
The PBE, Password Based Encryption, Algorithm, which is the Algorithm used to convert a given Passphrase to a Symmetric Key,
is based on the PBKDF2 algorithm, which again is a special way to generated a Symmetric Key, just as normal Symmetric Keys.
The allowed values are:
 * '''PBE_GCM_256'''

|Settings                                                                                                                                                 |
|account name|credential|key                     |value      |defined?|return code?          |return message?                                             |
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|eds.crypto.pbe.algorithm|PBE_CBC_128|PBE_GCM_256 |${SETTING_WARNING}|Unsupported Crypto Algorithm for 'eds.crypto.pbe.algorithm'.|
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|eds.crypto.pbe.algorithm|PBE_CBC_192|PBE_GCM_256 |${SETTING_WARNING}|Unsupported Crypto Algorithm for 'eds.crypto.pbe.algorithm'.|
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|eds.crypto.pbe.algorithm|PBE_CBC_256|PBE_GCM_256 |${SETTING_WARNING}|Unsupported Crypto Algorithm for 'eds.crypto.pbe.algorithm'.|
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|eds.crypto.pbe.algorithm|PBE_GCM_128|PBE_GCM_256 |${SETTING_WARNING}|Unsupported Crypto Algorithm for 'eds.crypto.pbe.algorithm'.|
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|eds.crypto.pbe.algorithm|PBE_GCM_192|PBE_GCM_256 |${SETTING_WARNING}|Unsupported Crypto Algorithm for 'eds.crypto.pbe.algorithm'.|
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|eds.crypto.pbe.algorithm|PBE_GCM_256|PBE_GCM_256 |${SUCCESS}        |Ok                                                          |
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|eds.crypto.pbe.algorithm|PBE_GCM_512|PBE_GCM_256 |${SETTING_WARNING}|Unsupported Crypto Algorithm for 'eds.crypto.pbe.algorithm'.|
*!

!* Sanitized
[[ Top ][#content]]
!anchor sanitized
!4 '''Sanitized'''
Any server relies on the storage for correctness. If the storage used has flaws and the stored data is being altered as a consequence of this, then
it may have drastic consequences. Something which is encrypted may be rendered unreadable of just a single bit has been flipped. It is therefore
essential that the storage is always correct. To help with this, EDS has a feature build-in, which runs sanitizing checks at frequent interval,
so all data will be checked at least once every x days, where x is defined as a system property (eds.sanity.check.interval.days).

The sanitizing request is an administrative request, and the result is a list of Data Id's, of the stored Objects where their checksums no longer
match the encrypted data. The check can be made generally or for a Circle of Trust or simply as a check if new errors have occurred since a certain
date.

 * Sanitized - Read current status
   * REST (POST) request is: ${REST_ROOT}/sanitized

|sanitized                                                                          |
|account name|credential|circle id|since     |failures?|return code?|return message?|
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|null     |null      |[]       |${SUCCESS}  |Ok             |
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|null     |2019-01-01|[]       |${SUCCESS}  |Ok             |
*!

!* Authenticated
[[ Top ][#content]]
!anchor authenticated
!4 '''Authenticated'''
EDS is designed as a backend system to be integrated into other systems, which opens
the question of authentication checks, how to ensure that the standard authentication
checks is aligned with EDS, so EDS can be used to store data securely.

The use-cases for the authentication mechanism is check if an account may access the
securely stored data or not. It is not designed nor intended to replace other
security mechanisms, such as 2FA of existing mechanisms. The check is simply here
to serve the purpose checking if accounts are aligned or not.

This alignment check is required, since the user credentials are needed to unlock
the keys internally. For this reason, the account should use a separate and different
credential to unlock the EDS account, to prevent that poor passwords are passed on to
also weaken the security of the EDS stored data.

 * Authenticated - Check Member Authentication
   * REST (POST) request is: ${REST_ROOT}/authenticated

|authenticated                                                                    |
|account name|credential|member id?|return code?|return message?                  |
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|admin_id  |${SUCCESS}  |admin successfully authenticated.|
*!

!* Members
[[ Top ][#content]]
!anchor members
!4 '''Members'''
Managing Members is a core part of the Management. The following features can be
performed with the current API:

 * Create Member - Creates a new Account with a given password
   * Only '''System Administrators''' may perform this
   * REST (POST) request is: ${REST_ROOT}/members/createMember
 * Invite Member - Creates an invitation, so a Member can update themselves
   * Only '''System Administrators''' may perform this
   * REST (POST) request is: ${REST_ROOT}/members/inviteMember
 * Login - Simple way to temporarily assign a !-SessionKey-! to an account
   * REST (POST) request is: ${REST_ROOT}/members/login
 * Logout - Remove the temporary !-SessionKey-! from accessing the account
   * REST (POST) request is: ${REST_ROOT}/members/logout
 * Alter Member Roles - Allows an Administrator to change a Members permissions
   * Only '''System Administrators''' may perform this
   * REST (POST) request is: ${REST_ROOT}/members/alterMember
 * Update Member - Allows a member to update their account & credentials
   * REST (POST) request is: ${REST_ROOT}/members/updateMember
 * Invalidate Member - Allows a member to invalidate their account, rendering it useless
   * REST (POST) request is: ${REST_ROOT}/members/invalidate
 * Delete Member - Removes a Member Account from the System permanently
   * REST (POST) request is: ${REST_ROOT}/members/deleteMember
 * Fetch Members - Retrieve a list of one or more Members
   * REST (POST) request is: ${REST_ROOT}/members/fetchMembers

Firstly, there are 2 ways to create accounts, both require system administrative
permissions. The first way is to run the CREATE action the second is to use the
INVITE action. The CREATE action requires that the new account is completely defined,
i.e. that the account name and credentials. The INVITE will just require the account
name and issue a one-time invitation token, which the new user uses to set their own
credentials. EDS only stores a keyed hash (HMAC) of the token, and the invitation expires
after the time set in '''eds.invitation.timeout.hours'''.

Once accounts are in usage, it may not be feasible to constantly provide both the
account name and credentials. Hence, it is possible to perform a LOGIN. This will
take an Account and an existing Session and link them together for a brief period of
time, how brief is defined via the settings. The session is then the only information
required to identify and unlock the account. Since the Session is thus used as both
an identification and authentication value, it must be guarded well. The Account should
by the end of a session invoke the LOGOUT.

It should be noted, that it is not possible to change the credentials for an Account
using the Session!

|process member                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|account name|credential       |credential type|action    |member id |public key|new account name|new credential|member role|member id?|invitation?       |return code?             |return message?                                                                    |
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|PASSPHRASE     |CREATE    |null      |null      |admin2          |${PASSPHRASE_2}|ADMIN      |admin2_id |null             |${SUCCESS}               |The Member 'admin2' was successfully added to EDS.                                 |
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|PASSPHRASE     |CREATE    |null      |null      |member1         |${PASSPHRASE_1}|STANDARD   |member1_id|null             |${SUCCESS}               |The Member 'member1' was successfully added to EDS.                                |
|member1     |${PASSPHRASE_1}  |null           |UPDATE    |null      |null      |null            |null          |null       |null      |null             |${SUCCESS}               |The Member 'member1' was successfully updated.                                     |
|member1     |${PASSPHRASE_1}  |null           |LOGIN     |null      |null      |null            |session_key   |null       |$login_member_id=|null             |${SUCCESS}               |The Member 'member1' has successfully logged in.                                   |
|null        |session_key      |null           |UPDATE    |null      |null      |null            |new_session   |null       |null      |null             |${VERIFICATION_WARNING}  |It is only permitted to update the credentials when authenticating with Passphrase.|
|null        |session_key      |SESSION        |LOGIN     |null      |null      |null            |new_session   |null       |$login_member_id=|null             |${SUCCESS}               |The Member 'member1' has successfully logged in.                                   |
|null        |new_session      |SESSION        |LOGIN     |null      |null      |null            |new_session   |null       |$login_member_id=|null             |${SUCCESS}               |The Member 'member1' has successfully logged in.                                   |
|null        |new_session      |SESSION        |CREATE    |null      |null      |user9           |${PASSPHRASE_9}|null       |null      |null             |${AUTHORIZATION_WARNING} |Members are not permitted to create new Accounts.                                  |
|member1     |${PASSPHRASE_1}  |PASSPHRASE     |INVALIDATE|null      |null      |null            |null          |null       |null      |null             |${SUCCESS}               |The Member 'member1' has been Invalidated.                                         |
|member1     |${PASSPHRASE_1}  |null           |UPDATE    |null      |null      |null            |null          |null       |null      |null             |${AUTHENTICATION_WARNING}|Cannot authenticate the Account from the given Credentials.                        |
|null        |new_session      |SESSION        |UPDATE    |null      |null      |null            |null          |null       |null      |null             |${AUTHENTICATION_WARNING}|No Session could be found.                                                         |
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|null           |DELETE    |member1_id|null      |null            |null          |null       |null      |null             |${SUCCESS}               |The Member 'member1' has successfully been deleted.                                |
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|null           |INVITE    |null      |null      |invitee         |null          |null       |invitee_id|invitee_invitation|${SUCCESS}               |An invitation was successfully issued for 'invitee'.                               |
|invitee     |invitee_invitation|INVITATION     |UPDATE    |null      |null      |invitee         |${INVITEE_PASSPHRASE}|null       |invitee_id|null             |${SUCCESS}               |The invitation was successfully processed for 'invitee'.                           |
|invitee     |invitee_invitation|INVITATION     |UPDATE    |null      |null      |invitee         |${INVITEE_PASSPHRASE}|null       |null      |null             |${VERIFICATION_WARNING}  |Account does not have an invitation pending.                                       |
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|PASSPHRASE     |DELETE    |invitee_id|null      |null            |null          |null       |null      |null             |${SUCCESS}               |The Member 'invitee' has successfully been deleted.                                |

A LOGOUT ends the Session it comes with, and leaves the other Sessions of the Member alone.

|process member                                                                                                           |
|account name|credential     |credential type|action|new credential|return code?             |return message?                               |
|user2       |${PASSPHRASE_2}|PASSPHRASE     |LOGIN |logout_a      |${SUCCESS}               |The Member 'user2' has successfully logged in.|
|user2       |${PASSPHRASE_2}|PASSPHRASE     |LOGIN |logout_b      |${SUCCESS}               |The Member 'user2' has successfully logged in.|

*!

!* Circles of Trust
[[ Top ][#content]]
!anchor circles
!4 '''Circles of Trust'''
Circles of Trust is a core part of EDS, as this is the grouping of Members or
''Trustees'', to facilitate sharing of information. There are no limits as to
who may create a Circle of Trust. Circles of Trust do not have an Owner, but
rather one or more Circle Administrators. The first Member to create a Circle
will automatically become the initial Circle Administrator - or if a Member Id
is given, then this Member will be the initial Circle Administrator.

Circles of Trust do not have much information initially - basically just their
name, which must be unique. Circles of Trust may also have an external Circle
Key, which means a shared Key that can be used by Trustees from a Client system.

 * Create Circle - Creates a new Circle of Trust in EDS
   * REST (POST) request is: ${REST_ROOT}/circles/createCircle
 * Update Circle - Allows the Circle of Trust to be renamed
   * REST (POST) request is: ${REST_ROOT}/circles/updateCircle
 * Delete Circle - Removes a Circle with all Trustees & Data from the System
   * REST (POST) request is: ${REST_ROOT}/circles/deleteCircle
 * Fetch Circles - Retrieves a list of Circles in the current EDS instance
   * REST (POST) request is: ${REST_ROOT}/circles/fetchCircles

|process circle                                                                                                                                                                                |
|account name|credential|action|circle id |circle name    |member id|circle key      |circle id?|return code?             |return message ?                                                    |
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|CREATE|null      |circle1        |user1_id |null            |circle1_id|${SUCCESS}               |The Circle 'circle1' was successfully created.                      |
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|CREATE|null      |circle1        |null     |null            |null      |${IDENTIFICATION_WARNING}|A Circle with the requested name already exists.                    |
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|CREATE|null      |circle2        |null     |null            |circle2_id|${SUCCESS}               |The Circle 'circle2' was successfully created.                      |
|user2       |${PASSPHRASE_2}|CREATE|null      |circle3        |null     |super secret key|circle3_id|${SUCCESS}               |The Circle 'circle3' was successfully created.                      |
|user2       |${PASSPHRASE_2}|CREATE|null      |circle5        |null     |null            |circle5_id|${SUCCESS}               |The Circle 'circle5' was successfully created.                      |
|user2       |${PASSPHRASE_2}|UPDATE|circle5_id|new Circle Name|null     |null            |null      |${SUCCESS}               |The Circle 'new Circle Name' was successfully updated.              |
|user2       |${PASSPHRASE_2}|DELETE|circle5_id|null           |null     |null            |null      |${SUCCESS}               |The Circle 'new Circle Name' has successfully been removed from EDS.|


The Fetch Circles request lists the Circles a Member is a Trustee of; the System Administrator gets all Circles. With the setting
!-eds.show.all.circles-! (default false), every Member gets all Circles. Only a Trustee of a Circle can retrieve its Circle Key.

|fetch circles                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|account name|credential|circles?                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |return code?|return message?|
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|[Circle{circleId='circle1_id', circleName='circle1', circleKey='null'}, Circle{circleId='circle2_id', circleName='circle2', circleKey='null'}]            |${SUCCESS}  |Ok             |
|user2       |${PASSPHRASE_2}|[Circle{circleId='circle3_id', circleName='circle3', circleKey='super secret key'}]|${SUCCESS}  |Ok             |
*!

!* Trustees
[[ Top ][#content]]
!anchor trustees
!4 '''Trustees'''
Trustees are the Members of a Circle of Trust, each with a trust level: READ, WRITE or ADMIN. The administrators of a
Circle add, alter and remove its Trustees.

 * Add Trustee
   * REST (POST) request is: ${REST_ROOT}/trustees/addTrustee
 * Alter Trustee
   * REST (POST) request is: ${REST_ROOT}/trustees/alterTrustee
 * Remove Trustee
   * REST (POST) request is: ${REST_ROOT}/trustees/removeTrustee
 * Fetch Trustees
   * REST (POST) request is: ${REST_ROOT}/trustees/fetchTrustees

|process trustee                                                                                                                                                              |
|account name|credential|action|circle id |member id|trust level|return code?|return message ?                                                                                |
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|ADD   |circle2_id|user2_id |WRITE      |${SUCCESS}  |The Member 'user2' was successfully added as trustee to 'circle2'.                              |
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|ADD   |circle2_id|user3_id |READ       |${SUCCESS}  |The Member 'user3' was successfully added as trustee to 'circle2'.                              |
|user2       |${PASSPHRASE_2}|ADD   |circle3_id|user1_id |WRITE      |${SUCCESS}  |The Member 'user1' was successfully added as trustee to 'circle3'.                              |
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|ALTER |circle2_id|user3_id |ADMIN      |${SUCCESS}  |The Trustee 'user3' has successfully been given the trust level 'ADMIN' in the Circle 'circle2'.|
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|ALTER |circle2_id|user3_id |READ       |${SUCCESS}  |The Trustee 'user3' has successfully been given the trust level 'READ' in the Circle 'circle2'. |

If a Fetch Members for a given User is invoked now, then the list of Circles which the Member is entrusted with will also be returned.

|fetch members                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
|account name|credential|member id|members?                                                                                   |circles?                                                               |return code?|return message?|
|user2       |${PASSPHRASE_2}|user3_id |[Member{memberId='user3_id', accountName='user3', memberRole='STANDARD', publicKey='null'}]|[Circle{circleId='circle2_id', circleName='circle2', circleKey='null'}]|${SUCCESS}  |Ok             |

However, the Fetch Members request with the Circle listing is limited, and instead the fetch Trustees should be used, as it will
return a more accurate depiction of the relations. Note, that this request is more stringent in the results returned. System
Administrators are allowed to retrieve most information but members are only allowed to retrieve information if a relation between
the Member & Circle already exists.

|fetch trustees                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
|account name|credential|circle id |trustees?                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |return code?             |return message?                                                 |
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|circle3_id|[Trustee{memberId='user1_id', accountName='user1', circleId='circle3_id', circleName='null', trustLevel='WRITE', publicKey='null'}, Trustee{memberId='user2_id', accountName='user2', circleId='circle3_id', circleName='null', trustLevel='ADMIN', publicKey='null'}]|${SUCCESS}               |Ok                                                              |
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|circle3_id|[Trustee{memberId='user1_id', accountName='user1', circleId='circle3_id', circleName='null', trustLevel='WRITE', publicKey='null'}, Trustee{memberId='user2_id', accountName='user2', circleId='circle3_id', circleName='null', trustLevel='ADMIN', publicKey='null'}]|${SUCCESS}               |Ok                                                              |
|user2       |${PASSPHRASE_2}|circle3_id|[Trustee{memberId='user1_id', accountName='user1', circleId='circle3_id', circleName='null', trustLevel='WRITE', publicKey='null'}, Trustee{memberId='user2_id', accountName='user2', circleId='circle3_id', circleName='null', trustLevel='ADMIN', publicKey='null'}]|${SUCCESS}               |Ok                                                              |
|user3       |${PASSPHRASE_3}|circle3_id|[]                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |${IDENTIFICATION_WARNING}|=~/No Trustee information found for member 'user3' and circle.*/|

A Trustee may have a secret in a Circle: text of a client, which !-EDS-! stores without looking inside, for clients
which encrypt themselves (see E2E.md). Every Trustee sets their own with Alter Trustee, without a trust level; an administrator
of the Circle may set that of any Trustee.

|process trustee                                                                                                                                                         |
|account name|credential     |action|circle id |member id|secret           |return code?            |return message?                                                               |
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|ALTER |circle3_id|user1_id |wrapped-for-user1|${SUCCESS}              |The secret of the Trustee 'user1' in the Circle 'circle3' was successfully set.|
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|ALTER |circle3_id|user2_id |not-mine-to-set  |${AUTHORIZATION_WARNING}|Only an administrator of the Circle may set the secret of another Trustee.    |
|user2       |${PASSPHRASE_2}|ALTER |circle3_id|user2_id |wrapped-for-user2|${SUCCESS}              |The secret of the Trustee 'user2' in the Circle 'circle3' was successfully set.|

A secret is returned to its Member and to the administrators of the Circle, and to nobody else, also not to the System Administrator.

|fetch trustees                                                                                         |
|account name|credential         |circle id |secrets?                                                   |return code?|
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}    |circle3_id|[user1='wrapped-for-user1', user2='null']                  |${SUCCESS}  |
|user2       |${PASSPHRASE_2}    |circle3_id|[user1='wrapped-for-user1', user2='wrapped-for-user2']     |${SUCCESS}  |
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|circle3_id|[user1='null', user2='null']                               |${SUCCESS}  |

A client which keeps a key of its own in the secrets changes it for all Trustees at once, e.g. after a Trustee was removed:
Set Secrets (${REST_ROOT}/trustees/setSecrets) sets the secrets of several Trustees, and the external key of the Circle if
given, all or none. It needs the trust level ADMIN in the Circle; Trustees not named keep their secret.

|process trustee                                                                                                                                                                       |
|account name|credential         |action |circle id |secrets                              |circle key |return code?             |return message?                                                    |
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}    |SECRETS|circle3_id|user1_id=v2-user1, user2_id=v2-user2 |null       |${AUTHORIZATION_WARNING} |=~/not permitted/                                                  |
|user2       |${PASSPHRASE_2}    |SECRETS|circle3_id|user1_id=v2-user1, admin_id=v2-admin |null       |${IDENTIFICATION_WARNING}|=~/is not a Trustee of the Circle; no secret was set./             |
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|SECRETS|circle3_id|user1_id=v2-user1                    |null       |${ILLEGAL_ACTION}        |It is not possible to set secrets in a Circle, without membership. |

Nothing was set by the refused requests.

|fetch trustees                                                                                     |
|account name|credential     |circle id |secrets?                                               |return code?|
|user2       |${PASSPHRASE_2}|circle3_id|[user1='wrapped-for-user1', user2='wrapped-for-user2'] |${SUCCESS}  |

|process trustee                                                                                                                                                             |
|account name|credential     |action |circle id |secrets                              |circle key  |return code?|return message?                                                            |
|user2       |${PASSPHRASE_2}|SECRETS|circle3_id|user1_id=v2-user1, user2_id=v2-user2 |key v2      |${SUCCESS}  |The secrets of 2 Trustee(s) of the Circle 'circle3' were successfully set.|

|fetch trustees                                                                         |
|account name|credential     |circle id |secrets?                                 |return code?|
|user2       |${PASSPHRASE_2}|circle3_id|[user1='v2-user1', user2='v2-user2']     |${SUCCESS}  |

|fetch circles                                                                                                                                                      |
|account name|credential     |circles?                                                                                                                       |return code?|
|user2       |${PASSPHRASE_2}|[Circle{circleId='circle2_id', circleName='circle2', circleKey='null'}, Circle{circleId='circle3_id', circleName='circle3', circleKey='key v2'}]|${SUCCESS}  |

The administrators of a Circle remove its Trustees, and every Trustee may leave a Circle. The last Trustee can't leave it, as
nobody could read its data again; the Circle is deleted instead.

|process trustee                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|account name|credential     |action|circle id |member id|trust level|return code?            |return message?                                                                                                        |
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|ADD   |circle1_id|user2_id |READ       |${SUCCESS}              |The Member 'user2' was successfully added as trustee to 'circle1'.                                                     |
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|ADD   |circle1_id|user3_id |READ       |${SUCCESS}              |The Member 'user3' was successfully added as trustee to 'circle1'.                                                     |
|user3       |${PASSPHRASE_3}|REMOVE|circle1_id|user2_id |null       |${AUTHORIZATION_WARNING}|=~/not permitted/                                                                                                      |
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|REMOVE|circle1_id|user2_id |null       |${SUCCESS}              |The Trustee 'user2' was successfully removed from the Circle 'circle1'.                                                |
|user3       |${PASSPHRASE_3}|REMOVE|circle1_id|user3_id |null       |${SUCCESS}              |The Trustee 'user3' was successfully removed from the Circle 'circle1'.                                                |
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|REMOVE|circle1_id|user1_id |null       |${ILLEGAL_ACTION}       |The last Member of the Circle 'circle1' can't leave it, as nobody could read its data again. Delete the Circle instead.|

'''Rotating the Circle Secret.''' A Member who leaves a Circle, or is removed, loses their copy of the Circle Secret, but may
have kept what a client held of it. So the Circle Secret is rotated afterwards: the Circle gets a new secret, wrapped for every
Trustee, and its Data Objects are re-encrypted with it in the background, while everything reads and writes as before. The
stone can't read a Circle Secret by itself, so the rotation starts at the next request of a Trustee which reads it; above,
user2 and user3 left circle1, and its rotation starts with the next Data Object user1 adds to it (below). A rotation is also
due a period after the last one (''eds.circle.secret.rotation.days''), and a Circle administrator may ask for one: Rotate
Circle, ${REST_ROOT}/circles/rotateCircle.

|process circle                                                                                                                            |
|account name|credential     |action|circle id |circle name|member id|circle key|circle id?|return code?            |return message ?                                     |
|user3       |${PASSPHRASE_3}|ROTATE|circle2_id|null       |null     |null      |null      |${AUTHORIZATION_WARNING}|Only a Circle Administrator may perform this action.|
*!

!* Status
[[ Top ][#content]]
!anchor status
!4 '''Status'''
The Status tells those who look after a stone how it is doing: its load, how busy it is, and its inventory, what it holds,
in general numbers only (see STATUS.md). Like the Resource API, it takes the ''Authorization: Bearer'' header and answers
with the return code as HTTP status. The header carries either the Session of the System Administrator, or a status key:
a key which reads the status and nothing else, also while the stone is locked. The System Administrator creates the
status keys, each with a label; a key is returned once, as EDS keeps only its hash.

 * Status - ${REST_ROOT}/status (GET)
 * Status keys - ${REST_ROOT}/status/keys (GET, POST), ${REST_ROOT}/status/keys/{label} (DELETE)

|process member                                                     |
|account name|credential         |action|new credential|return code?|
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|LOGIN |sadmin_session|${SUCCESS}  |
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}    |LOGIN |suser1_session|${SUCCESS}  |

|resources                                                                                                                  |
|credential    |operation      |name   |new key    |status?|return code?             |names?   |awake?|version?    |samples?|
|sadmin_session|getStatus      |null   |null       |200    |${SUCCESS}               |null     |true  |2.0-SNAPSHOT|true    |
|suser1_session|getStatus      |null   |null       |401    |${AUTHORIZATION_WARNING} |null     |null  |null        |null    |
|null          |getStatus      |null   |null       |403    |${AUTHENTICATION_WARNING}|null     |null  |null        |null    |
|suser1_session|postStatusKey  |monitor|null       |401    |${AUTHORIZATION_WARNING} |null     |null  |null        |null    |
|sadmin_session|postStatusKey  |monitor|monitor_key|200    |${SUCCESS}               |[monitor]|null  |null        |null    |
|sadmin_session|postStatusKey  |monitor|null       |404    |${IDENTIFICATION_WARNING}|null     |null  |null        |null    |
|sadmin_session|postStatusKey  |null   |null       |406    |${VERIFICATION_WARNING}  |null     |null  |null        |null    |
|sadmin_session|getStatusKeys  |null   |null       |200    |${SUCCESS}               |[monitor]|null  |null        |null    |
|monitor_key   |getStatus      |null   |null       |200    |${SUCCESS}               |null     |true  |2.0-SNAPSHOT|true    |
|monitor_key   |getStatusKeys  |null   |null       |403    |${AUTHENTICATION_WARNING}|null     |null  |null        |null    |

A withdrawn key is refused from then on.

|resources                                                                    |
|credential    |operation      |name   |status?|return code?             |names?|
|sadmin_session|deleteStatusKey|monitor|200    |${SUCCESS}               |[]    |
|monitor_key   |getStatus      |null   |403    |${AUTHENTICATION_WARNING}|null  |
|sadmin_session|deleteStatusKey|monitor|404    |${IDENTIFICATION_WARNING}|null  |
*!

----
[[ Top ][#content]]
!anchor sharing
!2 Sharing

!* !-DataType-!
!anchor datatype
!4 '''Data Type'''
Since all data is stored in EDS encrypted, and EDS only cares that the bytes which
came in, also goes out - it can be hard for an application or server using EDS to
ascertain what is behind the bytes. For this reason, EDS supports storing data with
a "data type".

Data Types can be anything; by default 4 types exist: "folder", "data", "thumbnail",
the small image of a Data Object, and "entry", the entries of a feature, such as the
messages of a chat. If nothing is explicitly defined, the "data" will always be picked.
The "folder" is simply there to provide the possibility to have structures of data, and it
has the unique feature that Data Objects can have a folder as parent. All Circles of Trust will have a standard
folder as their root, and it is used transparently within EDS.

Working with data types requires administrative permissions, the request must be made
as either system administrator or circle administrator. In the example below, admin is
a system administrator, user1 is a circle administrator and user2 is neither.

!-<img src="files/note.png" align="left">-! Contrary to all other entities in EDS, data types do not have any id's, they
only have a name and a custom definition. The name is therefore unique, and is used to change or delete the Data Type.

There are 3 kinds of actions / requests which can be made for data Types
 * Process !-DataType-!
   * REST (POST) request is: ${REST_ROOT}/dataTypes/processDataType
 * Delete !-DataType-!
   * REST (POST) request is: ${REST_ROOT}/dataTypes/deleteDataType
 * Fetch !-DataTypes-!
   * REST (POST) request is: ${REST_ROOT}/dataTypes/fetchDataTypes

|process dataType                                                                                                                                                   |
|account name|credential|action |name          |type                         |return code?            |return message?                                              |
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|PROCESS|MIMEType PDF  |application/pdf              |${SUCCESS}              |The Data Type 'MIMEType PDF' was successfully processed.     |
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|PROCESS|jsonObject    |{"a":"b","c":"d"}            |${SUCCESS}              |The Data Type 'jsonObject' was successfully processed.       |
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|PROCESS|Object42      |com.company.object.ObjectName|${SUCCESS}              |The Data Type 'Object42' was successfully processed.         |
|user3       |${PASSPHRASE_3}|PROCESS|Awesome Object|Cool                         |${AUTHORIZATION_WARNING}|The requesting Account is not permitted to Process Data Type.|
|user3       |${PASSPHRASE_3}|DELETE |MIMEType PDF  |                             |${AUTHORIZATION_WARNING}|The requesting Account is not permitted to Process Data Type.|
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|DELETE |MIMEType PDF  |null                         |${SUCCESS}              |The Data Type 'MIMEType PDF' was successfully deleted.       |

|fetch dataTypes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
|account name|credential|data types?                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |return code?|return message?|
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|!-[DataType{typeName='folder', type='Folder'}, DataType{typeName='data', type='Data Object'}, DataType{typeName='thumbnail', type='Thumbnail'}, DataType{typeName='entry', type='Entry of a Feature'}, DataType{typeName='jsonObject', type='{"a":"b","c":"d"}'}, DataType{typeName='Object42', type='com.company.object.ObjectName'}]-!|${SUCCESS}  |Ok             |
*!

!* Data
[[ Top ][#content]]
!anchor data
!4 '''Data'''

 * Add Data to a Circle of Trust
   * REST (POST) request is: ${REST_ROOT}/data/addData
 * Copy Data from one Circle of Trust to another
   * REST (POST) request is: ${REST_ROOT}/data/copyData
 * Move Data from one Circle of Trust to another
   * REST (POST) request is: ${REST_ROOT}/data/moveData
 * Update Data record in a Circle of Trust
   * REST (POST) request is: ${REST_ROOT}/data/updateData
 * Delete Data record from a Circle of Trust
   * REST (POST) request is: ${REST_ROOT}/data/deleteData
 * Fetch Data from a Circle of Trust
   * REST (POST) request is: ${REST_ROOT}/data/fetchData

|process data                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|account name|credential|action|circle id |data id  |data name|type name     |target folder id|target circle id|data               |return code?        |return message?                                                             |
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|ADD   |circle1_id|null     |data1    |folder        |null            |null            |null               |${SUCCESS}          |The Folder 'data1' was successfully added to the Circle 'circle1'.          |
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|ADD   |circle1_id|null     |data2    |data          |null            |null            |First Data Object  |${SUCCESS}          |The Data Object 'data2' was successfully added to the Circle 'circle1'.     |
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|ADD   |circle2_id|null     |data3    |Awesome Object|null            |null            |Second Data Object |${INTEGRITY_WARNING}|Cannot find a matching !-DataType-! for the Object.                         |
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|DELETE|null      |data1_id |null     |null          |null            |null            |null               |${SUCCESS}          |The Data Object 'data1' has been removed from the Circle 'circle1'.         |
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|ADD   |circle1_id|null     |data4    |data          |null            |null            |Another Data Object|${SUCCESS}          |The Data Object 'data4' was successfully added to the Circle 'circle1'.     |
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|ADD   |circle1_id|null     |data5    |data          |null            |null            |More Data          |${SUCCESS}          |The Data Object 'data5' was successfully added to the Circle 'circle1'.     |
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|ADD   |circle2_id|null     |status   |null          |null            |null            |initial            |${SUCCESS}          |The Data Object 'status' was successfully added to the Circle 'circle2'.    |
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|UPDATE|circle2_id|status_id|null     |null          |null            |null            |updated content    |${SUCCESS}          |The Data Object 'status' was successfully updated.                          |
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|ADD   |circle2_id|null     |data6    |null          |null            |null            |some more data     |${SUCCESS}          |The Data Object 'data6' was successfully added to the Circle 'circle2'.     |
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|COPY  |circle2_id|data6_id |copied   |null          |null            |circle1_id      |null               |${SUCCESS}          |The Data Object 'data6' was successfully copied from 'circle2' to 'circle1'.|
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|MOVE  |circle2_id|data6_id |moved    |null          |null            |circle1_id      |null               |${SUCCESS}          |The Data Object 'data6' was successfully moved from 'circle2' to 'circle1'. |
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|UPDATE|circle1_id|copied_id|copied   |null          |null            |null            |null               |${SUCCESS}          |The Data Object 'copied' was successfully updated.                          |
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|UPDATE|circle1_id|moved_id |moved    |null          |null            |null            |null               |${SUCCESS}          |The Data Object 'moved' was successfully updated.                           |

|fetch data                                                                                                                                                                                             |
|account name|credential|circle id |data id  |data name|page number|page size|records?|folder id?     |data id?             |data name?     |type name?  |data?            |return code?|return message?|
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|circle1_id|null     |null     |1          |2        |5       |circle1_root_id|[moved_id, copied_id]|[moved, copied]|[data, data]|null             |${SUCCESS}  |Ok             |
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|circle1_id|null     |null     |2          |2        |5       |circle1_root_id|[data5_id, data4_id] |[data5, data4] |[data, data]|null             |${SUCCESS}  |Ok             |
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|null      |data2_id |null     |null       |null     |1       |circle1_root_id|data2_id             |data2          |data        |First Data Object|${SUCCESS}  |Ok             |
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|null      |null     |data2    |null       |null     |1       |circle1_root_id|data2_id             |data2          |data        |First Data Object|${SUCCESS}  |Ok             |
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|circle2_id|status_id|null     |null       |null     |1       |circle2_root_id|status_id            |status         |data        |updated content  |${SUCCESS}  |Ok             |

The !-MasterKey-! is rotated back to the original, with Members, Circles and Data in place. Data Objects aren't re-encrypted
by a rotation, so the data reads as before.

|master key                                                                                     |
|account name|credential         |url |secret              |return code?|return message?        |
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|null|${MASTERKEY_DEFAULT}|${SUCCESS}  |!-MasterKey-! updated. |

|fetch data                                                                                                                                                                                             |
|account name|credential|circle id |data id  |data name|page number|page size|records?|folder id?     |data id?             |data name?     |type name?  |data?            |return code?|return message?|
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|null      |data2_id |null     |null       |null     |1       |circle1_root_id|data2_id             |data2          |data        |First Data Object|${SUCCESS}  |Ok             |
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|circle2_id|status_id|null     |null       |null     |1       |circle2_root_id|status_id            |status         |data        |updated content  |${SUCCESS}  |Ok             |
*!

!* Content Streaming
[[ Top ][#content]]
!anchor streaming
!4 '''Content Streaming'''

Large content is sent and received as a raw stream, outside the JSON requests. The Data Object is registered first (without
data), then its content is uploaded. A download can ask for a byte range, so media can be played and seeked without loading
the whole object. Both authenticate with the Session token from a login (''Authorization: Bearer''), and answer with real
HTTP status codes. The content is encrypted in chunks (PLAN.md, Crypto §4), and only the chunks of a range are read and decrypted.

 * Upload Content - Replaces the content of a Data Object
   * REST (PUT) request is: ${REST_ROOT}/data/{dataId}/content
 * Download Content - The content, or a range of it
   * REST (GET) request is: ${REST_ROOT}/data/{dataId}/content
 * Content Headers - Size, ETag and type of the content
   * REST (HEAD) request is: ${REST_ROOT}/data/{dataId}/content

|process member                                                                                                    |
|account name|credential     |action|new credential|return code?|return message?                                 |
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|LOGIN |user1_session |${SUCCESS}  |The Member 'user1' has successfully logged in.   |

|process data                                                                                                     |
|account name|credential     |action|circle id |data name|type name|media type|return code?|
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|ADD   |circle1_id|stream1  |data     |video/mp4 |${SUCCESS}  |
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|ADD   |circle1_id|stream2  |data     |null      |${SUCCESS}  |

|upload content                                                                                                                 |
|credential   |data id   |content                                    |generated size|if match|return code?            |etag?|
|user1_session|stream1_id|The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog|null          |null    |${SUCCESS}              |set  |
|user1_session|stream2_id|null                                       |200000        |null    |${SUCCESS}              |set  |
|user1_session|stream2_id|null                                       |10            |"stale" |${PRECONDITION_FAILED}  |null |
|null         |stream1_id|small                                      |null          |null    |${AUTHENTICATION_WARNING}|null |

The download of the text, in full and in ranges. The media type ''video/mp4'' may be shown inline; the content without a
media type is served for download only.

|download content                                                                                                                                                    |
|credential   |data id   |range        |if range|head |status?|content?                                   |content length?|content range?|content type?           |disposition?|
|user1_session|stream1_id|null         |null    |false|200    |The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog|43             |null          |video/mp4               |inline      |
|user1_session|stream1_id|bytes=4-8    |null    |false|206    |quick                                      |5              |bytes 4-8/43  |video/mp4               |inline      |
|user1_session|stream1_id|bytes=-3     |null    |false|206    |dog                                        |3              |bytes 40-42/43|video/mp4               |inline      |
|user1_session|stream1_id|bytes=4-8    |"stale" |false|200    |The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog|43             |null          |video/mp4               |inline      |
|user1_session|stream1_id|null         |null    |true |200    |null                                       |43             |null          |video/mp4               |inline      |

The larger content is checked against the generated bytes: in full, across the boundary of the first two chunks (64 KiB), and
the last byte. A range outside the content is not satisfiable (416).

|download content                                                                                                                                     |
|credential   |data id   |range            |status?|content length?|content range?            |matches generated?|content type?           |disposition?|return code?             |
|user1_session|stream2_id|null             |200    |200000         |null                      |true              |application/octet-stream|attachment  |${SUCCESS}               |
|user1_session|stream2_id|bytes=65530-65545|206    |16             |bytes 65530-65545/200000  |true              |application/octet-stream|attachment  |206                      |
|user1_session|stream2_id|bytes=199999-    |206    |1              |bytes 199999-199999/200000|true              |application/octet-stream|attachment  |206                      |
|user1_session|stream2_id|bytes=200000-    |416    |null           |bytes */200000            |null              |null                    |null        |${RANGE_NOT_SATISFIABLE} |
|null         |stream2_id|null             |403    |null           |null                      |null              |null                    |null        |${AUTHENTICATION_WARNING}|

'''Download tokens.''' The media elements of a browser (''img'', ''video'') can't send the ''Authorization'' header. A
download token, created with the Session, reads the content of this one Data Object instead, as the query parameter
''token''; ranges work as usual, so a player can seek. It reads no other Data Object, and ends at its expiry, at logout, or
when the !-MasterKey-! changes.

 * Create Download Token - ${REST_ROOT}/data/{dataId}/token (POST)
 * Download Content with a token - ${REST_ROOT}/data/{dataId}/content?token=... (GET, HEAD)

|resources                                                                       |
|credential   |operation          |data id   |new key|status?|return code?             |
|user1_session|createDownloadToken|stream1_id|token1 |200    |${SUCCESS}               |
|null         |createDownloadToken|stream1_id|null   |403    |${AUTHENTICATION_WARNING}|

|download content                                                                                                   |
|credential|data id   |token |range    |status?|content?                                   |content type?|return code?|
|null      |stream1_id|token1_id|bytes=4-8|206    |quick                                      |video/mp4    |206         |
|null      |stream1_id|token1_id|null     |200    |The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog|video/mp4    |${SUCCESS}  |

The token is bound to its Data Object, and an invalid token reads nothing.

|download content                                                       |
|credential|data id   |token      |status?|return code?             |
|null      |stream2_id|token1_id  |403    |${AUTHENTICATION_WARNING}|
|null      |stream1_id|not-a-token|403    |${AUTHENTICATION_WARNING}|

'''Thumbnails.''' A client (Rune draws them in the browser) stores a small image of the content, encrypted like any
content; EDS never reads it. The Metadata of the Data Object points to it (''thumbnailId''), it is downloaded like any
content, and new content removes it, as it no longer matches. Only JPEG, PNG and WebP are accepted; other media types
are refused by the HTTP layer (415, without a JSON body).

 * Store Thumbnail - ${REST_ROOT}/data/{dataId}/thumbnail (PUT)

|resources                                                                                                     |
|credential   |operation   |data id   |content        |media type   |new key|status?|return code?|thumbnail id?|
|user1_session|putThumbnail|stream1_id|thumbnail bytes|image/png    |thumb1 |200    |${SUCCESS}  |null         |
|user1_session|getDataById |stream1_id|null           |null         |null   |200    |${SUCCESS}  |thumb1_id    |

|download content                                                                             |
|credential   |data id|status?|content?       |content type?|disposition?|return code?|
|user1_session|thumb1_id|200    |thumbnail bytes|image/png    |inline      |${SUCCESS}  |

|upload content                                                                     |
|credential   |data id   |content    |generated size|if match|return code?|etag?|
|user1_session|stream1_id|new content|null          |null    |${SUCCESS}  |set  |

|resources                                                         |
|credential   |operation  |data id   |status?|thumbnail id?|
|user1_session|getDataById|stream1_id|200    |null         |

|process data                                                                       |
|account name|credential     |action|data id   |return code?|
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|DELETE|stream1_id|${SUCCESS}  |
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|DELETE|stream2_id|${SUCCESS}  |

|download content                                                       |
|credential   |data id   |status?|return code?             |
|user1_session|stream1_id|404    |${IDENTIFICATION_WARNING}|

!* Resource API
[[ Top ][#content]]
!anchor resources
!4 '''Resource API'''

Next to the JSON API, EDS has an ID-based resource API, where the IDs are part of the path, and the HTTP method says what to do.
Each operation runs the same rules as its JSON twin, with the same request object as body; values from the path replace those
of the body. It only accepts a Session, as ''Authorization: Bearer'', and answers with the return code as HTTP status. The
operations are named by their operationId in the API contract (''openapi.json'').

 * Members - ${REST_ROOT}/members (GET, POST), ${REST_ROOT}/members/{memberId} (GET, PUT, DELETE)
 * Circles - ${REST_ROOT}/circles (GET, POST), ${REST_ROOT}/circles/{circleId} (GET, PUT, DELETE)
 * Trustees - ${REST_ROOT}/circles/{circleId}/trustees (GET, POST), ${REST_ROOT}/circles/{circleId}/trustees/{memberId} (PUT, DELETE)
 * Data - ${REST_ROOT}/data?circleId= (GET), ${REST_ROOT}/data (POST), ${REST_ROOT}/data/{dataId} (GET, PUT, DELETE), ${REST_ROOT}/data/{dataId}/copy and /move (POST)
 * Data Types - ${REST_ROOT}/dataTypes (GET), ${REST_ROOT}/dataTypes/{typeName} (PUT, DELETE)

|process member                                                                                                    |
|account name|credential         |action|new credential|return code?|
|admin       |${ADMIN_PASSPHRASE}|LOGIN |admin_session |${SUCCESS}  |

The System Administrator creates a Member, and changes its role; a standard Member may not create Members.

|resources                                                                                                                  |
|credential   |operation       |member id  |name    |new credential |role |new key|status?|return code?             |names?|
|admin_session|postMembers     |null       |rmember |${PASSPHRASE_9}|null |rmember|200    |${SUCCESS}               |null|
|admin_session|getMemberById   |rmember_id |null    |null           |null |null   |200    |${SUCCESS}               |[rmember:STANDARD]|
|admin_session|putMemberById   |rmember_id |null    |null           |ADMIN|null   |200    |${SUCCESS}               |null|
|admin_session|getMemberById   |rmember_id |null    |null           |null |null   |200    |${SUCCESS}               |[rmember:ADMIN]|
|admin_session|putMemberById   |rmember_id |null    |null           |STANDARD|null|200    |${SUCCESS}               |null|
|user1_session|postMembers     |null       |rother  |${PASSPHRASE_9}|null |rother |401    |${AUTHORIZATION_WARNING} |null|

A Member creates two Circles, renames one, and adds the new Member as Trustee. An unknown Circle is ''404''.

|resources                                                                                                                         |
|credential   |operation              |circle id                           |member id |name            |trust level|new key|status?|return code?             |names?|
|user1_session|postCircles            |null                                |null      |rcircle         |null       |rcircle|200    |${SUCCESS}               |null|
|user1_session|postCircles            |null                                |null      |rtarget         |null       |rtarget|200    |${SUCCESS}               |null|
|user1_session|putCircleById          |rcircle_id                          |null      |rcircle renamed |null       |null   |200    |${SUCCESS}               |null|
|user1_session|getCircleById          |rcircle_id                          |null      |null            |null       |null   |200    |${SUCCESS}               |[rcircle renamed]|
|user1_session|getCircleById          |4c5bc2c6-0fa5-4c3a-9d1e-1a2b3c4d5e6f|null      |null            |null       |null   |404    |${IDENTIFICATION_WARNING}|[]    |
|user1_session|postCircleTrustees     |rcircle_id                          |rmember_id|null            |READ       |null   |200    |${SUCCESS}               |null|
|user1_session|getCircleTrustees      |rcircle_id                          |null      |null            |null       |null   |200    |${SUCCESS}               |[rmember:READ, user1:ADMIN]|
|user1_session|putCircleTrusteeById   |rcircle_id                          |rmember_id|null            |WRITE      |null   |200    |${SUCCESS}               |null|
|user1_session|getCircleTrustees      |rcircle_id                          |null      |null            |null       |null   |200    |${SUCCESS}               |[rmember:WRITE, user1:ADMIN]|

The secrets of several Trustees are set at once, all or none, as with Set Secrets: ${REST_ROOT}/circles/{circleId}/secrets (PUT).

|resources                                                                                                                       |
|credential   |operation       |circle id |secrets                                   |external key|status?|return code?             |
|user1_session|putCircleSecrets|rcircle_id|rmember_id=for-rmember, user2_id=for-user2|null        |404    |${IDENTIFICATION_WARNING}|
|user1_session|putCircleSecrets|rcircle_id|rmember_id=for-rmember, user1_id=for-user1|shared key  |200    |${SUCCESS}               |

|fetch trustees                                                                      |
|account name|credential     |circle id |secrets?                                  |return code?|
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|rcircle_id|[rmember='for-rmember', user1='for-user1']|${SUCCESS}  |

|resources                                                                                                                                                    |
|credential   |operation              |circle id |member id |name|trust level|new key|status?|return code?|names?       |
|user1_session|deleteCircleTrusteeById|rcircle_id|rmember_id|null|null       |null   |200    |${SUCCESS}  |null         |
|user1_session|getCircleTrustees      |rcircle_id|null      |null|null       |null   |200    |${SUCCESS}  |[user1:ADMIN]|

The rotation of the Circle Secret of circle1, which user1 started in the Data section, runs in the background; the Circle tells it
(''secretRotated'', ''rotationDue'' and ''rotation'' with its progress). When it has ended, the Data Objects read as before. A Circle
administrator has the secret of circle2 rotated now: ${REST_ROOT}/circles/{circleId}/rotation (PUT). The System Administrator
may ask too, but isn't a Trustee, so that rotation would start at the next request of a Trustee.

|resources                                                                                        |
|credential   |operation        |circle id |status?|return code?             |rotation due?|rotated?|
|user1_session|waitForRotation  |circle1_id|200    |${SUCCESS}               |set          |true    |
|user1_session|putCircleRotation|circle2_id|200    |${SUCCESS}               |null         |null    |
|user1_session|waitForRotation  |circle2_id|200    |${SUCCESS}               |set          |true    |
|null         |putCircleRotation|circle2_id|403    |${AUTHENTICATION_WARNING}|null         |null    |

|fetch data                                                                                                                                                           |
|account name|credential     |circle id |data id  |data name|page number|page size|records?|folder id?     |data id?|data name?|type name?|data?            |return code?|
|user1       |${PASSPHRASE_1}|null      |data2_id |null     |null       |null     |1       |circle1_root_id|data2_id|data2     |data      |First Data Object|${SUCCESS}  |
|user2       |${PASSPHRASE_2}|circle2_id|status_id|null     |null       |null     |1       |circle2_root_id|status_id|status   |data      |updated content  |${SUCCESS}  |

Data Objects are added, listed with their size, fetched without their content, renamed, copied and moved to the other Circle,
and deleted. A move gives the Data Object a new ID.

|resources                                                                                                                                         |
|credential   |operation     |circle id |data id |target circle id|name          |content     |new key|status?|return code?             |names?|size?|without content?|
|user1_session|postData      |rcircle_id|null    |null            |rnote         |twelve bytes|rnote  |200    |${SUCCESS}               |null|null|null|
|user1_session|getData       |rcircle_id|null    |null            |null          |null        |null   |200    |${SUCCESS}               |[rnote]|12   |true            |
|user1_session|getDataById   |null      |rnote_id|null            |null          |null        |null   |200    |${SUCCESS}               |[rnote]|12  |true            |
|user1_session|putDataById   |null      |rnote_id|null            |rnote renamed |null        |null   |200    |${SUCCESS}               |null|null|null|
|user1_session|postDataCopy  |null      |rnote_id|rtarget_id      |null          |null        |rcopy  |200    |${SUCCESS}               |null|null|null|
|user1_session|postDataMove  |null      |rnote_id|rtarget_id      |null          |null        |rmoved |200    |${SUCCESS}               |null|null|null|
|user1_session|getData       |rtarget_id|null    |null            |null          |null        |null   |200    |${SUCCESS}               |[rnote renamed, rnote renamed]|12|true|
|user1_session|getDataById   |null      |rcopy_id|null            |null          |null        |null   |200    |${SUCCESS}               |[rnote renamed]|12|true|
|user1_session|deleteDataById|null      |rcopy_id|null            |null          |null        |null   |200    |${SUCCESS}               |null|null|null|
|user1_session|deleteDataById|null      |rmoved_id|null           |null          |null        |null   |200    |${SUCCESS}               |null|null|null|
|user1_session|getData       |rtarget_id|null    |null            |null          |null        |null   |200    |${SUCCESS}               |[]    |null|true            |

Data Types are created or changed by their name, listed and deleted.

|resources                                                                                          |
|credential   |operation           |name |type               |status?|return code?|names?|
|user1_session|putDataTypeByName   |rtype|Resource test type |200    |${SUCCESS}  |null|
|user1_session|getDataTypes        |null |null               |200    |${SUCCESS}  |[Object42, data, entry, folder, jsonObject, rtype, thumbnail]|
|user1_session|deleteDataTypeByName|rtype|null               |200    |${SUCCESS}  |null|

Invalid requests and missing or unknown Sessions are answered with their HTTP status. Credentials in the body don't replace the
Session. At the end, the Circles and the Member are deleted.

|resources                                                                                          |
|credential     |operation       |circle id |member id |name|status?|return code?             |
|user1_session  |postCircles     |null      |null      |null|406    |${VERIFICATION_WARNING}  |
|null           |getCircles      |null      |null      |null|403    |${AUTHENTICATION_WARNING}|
|no_such_session|getCircles      |null      |null      |null|403    |${AUTHENTICATION_WARNING}|
|user1_session  |deleteCircleById|rcircle_id|null      |null|200    |${SUCCESS}               |
|user1_session  |deleteCircleById|rtarget_id|null      |null|200    |${SUCCESS}               |
|admin_session  |deleteMemberById|null      |rmember_id|null|200    |${SUCCESS}               |
|admin_session  |getMemberById   |null      |4c5bc2c6-0fa5-4c3a-9d1e-1a2b3c4d5e6f|null|404|${IDENTIFICATION_WARNING}|

The Member is gone from the listing of all Members.

|resources                                                                                       |
|credential   |operation |status?|names?                                                              |
|admin_session|getMembers|200    |[admin2:ADMIN, admin:ADMIN, user1:STANDARD, user2:STANDARD, user3:STANDARD]|
